key_insight: MACE-driven molecular dynamics reproduces overall DFT sorption trends for defects in 2D materials, with qualitative trends largely unchanged at 300 K.
engineering_relevance: Low-cost ML-driven simulations enable high-throughput prescreening of defect sorption behavior before expensive first-principles validation.
method: Evaluate 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database.
Use the MACE machine learning interatomic potential for simulations at 0 K and 300 K.
Compare adsorption-versus-absorption trends with prior high-throughput DFT results.
evidence_signal: Across 17,624 structures, MACE reproduced overall DFT sorption trends at 0 K at a fraction of the computational cost, while 300 K simulations retained largely similar qualitative trends.
watch_item: Agreement in aggregate sorption trends does not establish quantitative accuracy or long-term defect stability; DFT validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
